date.as_written: kāle dyocāraṇavikalite, śuddhanepālaśāke, māghe māse śaśadharadine ... śrīpañcamyāṃ ... śukle pakṣe

notes: The year is given as a word-numeral chronogram, 'dyocāraṇavikalite', which looks corrupt. 'dyo' (sky) normally stands for 0, but the other elements can't be read with confidence. The year 906 comes from the catalogue and can't be checked against this text. The verb is 'lekhayāmāsa' ('had it written'), so Cakrarāja is literally the commissioner. The catalogue lists him as scribe; he may have been both. 'dharaṇivibudha' ('god on earth') means a brāhmaṇa. 'sudhīra' ('steadfast') is an epithet. The final 'kena' is probably a corruption, maybe of 'kenāpi' or a metrical filler. Śrīpañcamī falls on Māgha śukla 5.
